question: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but very poor room-temperature ductility, while its irradiation resistance has primarily been proposed by first-principles calculations. What intervention could improve its room-temperature ductility without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the untreated NbMoTaW baseline under room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation assessments, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a falsification experiment.
